..
The relatively dry trade-wind regime continues, keeping shower 
chances topped at 20 percent throughout the entire forecast period, 
with the exception of 30 percent on Friday for Guam. Transient
trade-wind troughs will continue to move through the islands,
possibly bringing a slight uptick in showers here and there. Looking
ahead, there is the possibility for a stronger trough to pass south
of the region, with its outermost showers settling over Guam, mainly
concentrated over southern portions of the island. Since this is
still six days ahead, much can change from here on out.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Guam is abnormally dry (D0)
while the CNMI is unchanged. A strong to very-strong El Nino remains
the dominant climate oscillation, meaning a possible earlier onset of
drought, as well as the continued potential for tropical cyclones. 
Water conservation is highly encouraged sooner rather than later, 
especially as dry season approaches. Maintain general storm 
preparedness and weather awareness.

Marine/Surf...
Moderate trade winds will prevail through Monday night, becoming 
moderate to fresh throughout the rest of the forecast period. 
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are comprised of a north swell and a 
trade swell. Seas will diminish over the next few days but may 
increase back to 6 to 8 feet around the end of next week due to a
building trade swell. There is a moderate risk of rip currents along 
north- and east-facing reefs and a low risk elsewhere at least through
Monday night. The north swell may diminish below 2 feet around mid-
week before the trade swell increases, possibly up to 7 feet before 
next weekend.

Eastern Micronesia...
The weather remains dry and quiet, although the remnants of Tropical
Storm Pena are easily east-southeast of Majuro. This feature is along
an east-west Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) that stretches from near
Nukuoro in the FSM (Federated States of Micronesia) to the
circulation (somewhat broad) northeast of Makin in the southern RMI 
(Republic of the Marshall Islands)/east-southeast of Majuro. The 
models show this wave moving west along the NET, while potentially 
helping lift the NET north slightly as its orientation is locally 
augmented. Additionally, the Galvez-Davison Index (GDI) climbs above
50, indicative of scattered shower potential. Various runs of the 
GFS and ECMWF indicate this, with precipitation signatures suggesting
scattered showers as well. This increased rainfall coverage/potential
is anticipated to develop during the latter half of the week and 
into next weekend.

As for marine conditions, look for mainly light to gentle winds to
prevail area-wide, although brief afternoon periods of gentle to 
moderate winds may develop, mainly at Pohnpei towards the latter half
of the week. Seas will be in the 4 to 6 foot range.

Most of eastern Micronesia is experiencing abnormally dry (D0) drought
conditions. Try to conserve water as we continue to transition into 
the dry season.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows isolated to scattered showers throughout the
region. These showers are expected to be short-lived with low 
rainfall totals. Overall, mostly benign weather with few intermittent
showers are expected throughout the rest of the week.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Yap and Chuuk are abnormally 
dry (D0) while Palau is in a moderate drought (D1). A strong to 
very-strong El Nino remains the dominant climate oscillation, meaning
a possible earlier onset of drought, as well as the continued 
potential for tropical cyclones. Water conservation is highly 
encouraged sooner rather than later, especially as dry season 
approaches. Maintain general storm preparedness and weather 
awareness.

The north swell continues slowly subsiding. Combined seas of 5 to 7
feet will gradually fall to around 4 to 5 feet by Monday night. 
Starting around Tuesday the north swell is anticipated to shift to 
northeast and build to around 7 feet. This will build surf to 7 to 8
feet. While seas and surf are expected to build, they are expected to
remain below advisory thresholds of 10 foot seas and 9 foot surf.
Light to moderate winds are expected to build to gentle to fresh for
the middle of the week before tapering down to light to moderate for
the weekend.
